CYP2D6 is highly polymorphic — poor metabolizers (PMs, ~5-10% of Caucasians) lack functional enzyme, while ultra-rapid metabolizers carry gene duplications, creating large inter-individual variability in drug exposure.

The CYP2D6 active site is a relatively small, elongated cavity with a key negatively charged residue (Asp301) at the entrance that forms an ion pair or hydrogen bond with basic nitrogen atoms in substrates. The heme iron is at the base. This acidic residue is the defining selectivity feature — it creates a strong preference for basic, cationic substrates.

A planar hydrophobic region (usually an aromatic ring) adjacent to the metabolic site that fits into the hydrophobic pocket of the active site. Many CYP2D6 substrates share a common pharmacophoric pattern: basic N—(2-3 carbon linker)—aromatic ring with the oxidation occurring on or near the aromatic ring. Moderate lipophilicity (logP 1-4). Molecular weight 200-500 Da.

Features arguing against CYP2D6 metabolism: absence of a basic nitrogen — acidic, neutral, or non-ionizable compounds are generally not CYP2D6 substrates. Very large, bulky molecules (MW > 500) cannot fit the small active site. Compounds with no aromatic ring or the aromatic ring too far from the basic nitrogen.
